name: ZealousSwap token cell (KCC-0020 State, KCC-1 tag dispatch)

review.note: ZealousSwap's current-generation token cell on testnet-10 (2026-09-05), decoded from chain bytes only: the 2,590 B program carries the KCC-0020 State layout at offset 1 (amount, owner, owner scheme, borrow scheme, guard, extension commitment); every launch's curve and pool carry this template hash as their token template. Dispatch is a 4-byte tag before the program, compared in program order: transfer_whole, transfer, merge, the borrowed receive, transfer_delegator; any other tag falls to OP_RETURN. The tags do not reproduce from KCC-1 dispatch of the names and types listed here, which are kascov's reading of the argument layouts (the venue's names are unknown), so they are pin knowledge read from the bytes. Four were read from 535 spends of two launches (WBLF, ROCKET); the borrowed receive (a85e5b91) was read from the bytes alone and no spend on chain has used it. Reviewed 2026-09-06 on two legs, with no source leg because the venue has published none. Bytes to chain: both fixtures are leader reveals fetched from testnet-10, differ only in the state window, and recompute this template hash, so what is described here is what runs on chain. Bytes: every arm was read instruction by instruction. Owner authentication is one block shared by the four owner-signed arms, keyed on the cell's own scheme byte: 0x00 CheckSig by the owner key; 0x01 the revealed 32-byte key must hash to the owner under KCC-2's keyed BLAKE3 ('PublicKeyHash') and sign; 0x03 the input named by the small argument must spend the P2SH whose script hash is the owner; 0x04 the named input must carry the owner as its covenant id, and a cell may never be owned by its own family. Scheme 0x02 has no arm and no successor may carry it. Every successor is computed by the program from its own state and the arguments, never read from an output, and each successor program is rebuilt from the leader's own signature script (the 1-byte prefix and the 2,477-byte suffix by OpTxInputScriptSigSubstr) and must equal the bound output's BLAKE2b P2SH: transfer needs exactly one family input and two bound outputs, k=0 the declared recipient (amount strictly between 0 and the balance, class inherited, owner scheme in {0,1,3,4} with 0x04 never the family's own id, borrow scheme in 0..=3, any guard) and k=1 the leader's own state minus the amount; transfer_whole moves the whole amount to a declared owner the same way; merge needs exactly two family inputs with this cell first, reads the follower's six state fields out of the follower's revealed program at fixed offsets from its end, requires the same class, and binds one output carrying the sum under the leader's own owner, scheme, borrow scheme and guard; the borrowed receive needs exactly two family inputs, this cell first with a borrow scheme other than 0x00 and the follower's class, takes an amount, a 32-byte slot, a 65-byte slot and the follower's remainder, checks the rule per scheme (0x01: the int in guard bytes 0..8, read by OpBin2Num, must be non-negative (negative zero reads as 0 and passes) and the amount must strictly exceed it; 0x02: CheckSig by the guard as a key over the 65-byte slot; 0x03: BLAKE3 of the 32-byte slot equals the guard and the successor's guard becomes that preimage), requires amount plus remainder to equal the follower's amount (a zero remainder is legal, so this arm can leave a zero-amount cell), and binds k=0 the leader grown by the amount and k=1 the follower's state at the remainder; transfer_delegator needs at least two family inputs with this cell not first, its owner's authentication and no bound output, and reads the leader's state without constraining it. KAS floors: a transfer's change cell, and the single or first output of the other arms, may not hold less KAS than the spent cell; recipient and remainder cells have no floor. Arithmetic is the engine's checked i64. Conservation therefore holds by construction inside the program, and the family is closed: with three or more family inputs no leader arm accepts the count, a follower can never bind an output, and every output the program binds is this template again. Engine: the fixture program was exercised by the real Kaspa script engine with the covenant context (crates/kascov-labkit/src/kcc0020_zealous.rs) on every rule above, all four owner schemes on the spending side and the three borrow schemes including a two-step hash chain, and the program itself rejected a transfer of zero, of the whole balance or above it, a forged change or recipient cell, a fresh class, a change cell handed to another owner, swapped continuations, successor schemes 0x02 and 0x05 and borrow scheme 0x04, a successor owned by the family, a foreign signature, a wrong-width slot, a key that does not hash to a p2pkh owner, the right key with a foreign signature, an authority input that is not the owner script or covenant, a minting or burning whole, a minting or misowned merge, a cross-class merge, a transfer with a follower present, three family inputs, a delegator posing as leader or standing alone, a follower binding an output, an unknown tag, a threshold-equal borrow, an unconserved remainder, a borrow into a disabled cell, a foreign borrow key, a forged, stale or replayed hash-chain preimage, and every reduced KAS floor. Signature validity stays consensus's: the engine checked it in the ladder, kascov's reader does not re-run sighash on chain data (a guard-key borrow is judged structurally, threshold and hash chain from bytes). Bounds are the program's own (two family inputs, two bound outputs). The reader derives the borrowed receive's two successors the same hash-gated way as the other arms.
